1.title: Databases
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Databases. This module covers task statement three point four, identifying the A W S database services. You will learn when to run a database yourself and when to let A W S manage it, which engine fits which kind of data, and how to migrate a database to A W S. Most questions give you a need and ask you to name the database service.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Explain why a managed database, such as Amazon R D S, beats one you run on E C two. Tell Multi-A Z deployments from read replicas, and say what Amazon Aurora adds. Recognize Amazon Dynamo D B for no S Q L, and Amazon ElastiCache for in-memory speed. Place Amazon Document D B and Amazon Neptune. And use A W S D M S and A W S S C T to migrate a database.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater's Data Needs Differ
1.text: Tidewater's data needs differ. The order database runs on a server the team patches and backs up itself, often on weekends. The product catalog needs simple lookups in milliseconds, even at the sale peak. The same popular product pages are read thousands of times a minute. A recommendation idea needs to follow links between customers, orders and products. And an old Oracle database must move to A W S with little downtime. Your job is to choose the database for each need.

1.title: Database Types at a Glance
1.text: Start with the data model, because it points to the service. Relational databases store data in tables and are queried with S Q L. That is Amazon R D S and Amazon Aurora. Key-value no S Q L databases give simple, fast lookups at any scale. That is Amazon Dynamo D B. Document databases store J S O N-like documents and, in A W S, are compatible with Mongo D B. That is Amazon Document D B. In-memory stores hold data and caches in memory. That is Amazon ElastiCache. And graph databases follow relationships between things. That is Amazon Neptune. Exam tip: name the data model first: tables, key-value, documents, memory or relationships.

1.title: Self-Managed or Managed: Databases on EC2 and Amazon RDS
1.text: You can run a database yourself on E C two, or let A W S manage it with Amazon Relational Database Service, or R D S. Compare who does what. Installing and patching the database software: on E C two that is you; on R D S it is A W S. Patching the operating system: you on E C two, A W S on R D S. Backups, scaling and high availability: you on E C two, A W S on R D S. Query tuning and application design: you in both cases. And hardware, power and cooling: A W S in both cases. R D S runs Db two, Maria D B, S Q L Server, My S Q L, Oracle and Postgres S Q L, plus Aurora, and A W S recommends it as the default for most relational workloads. Exam tip: less administration means Amazon R D S; full control of the database server means E C two.

1.title: RDS Multi-AZ and Read Replicas
1.text: Two R D S features are easy to confuse. A Multi-A Z deployment is for availability. R D S keeps a standby in another Availability Zone, copied synchronously, and fails over automatically if the primary fails. In a Multi-A Z D B instance deployment, the standby does not serve reads, though a Multi-A Z D B cluster has readable standbys. Read replicas are for scaling reads. They are read-only copies, updated asynchronously, so they take reporting and read-heavy traffic off the primary. A replica can live in another Region, and it can be promoted to a standalone instance for disaster recovery. R D S does not autoscale replicas; you create them. Look at the figure. Exam tip: availability and failover mean Multi-A Z; read scaling means read replicas.

1.title: Amazon Aurora: Relational Built for the Cloud
1.text: Amazon Aurora is a fully managed relational engine that is compatible with My S Q L and Postgres S Q L. It is part of Amazon R D S, so the same console, C L I and A P I handle provisioning, patching, backup, recovery and failure detection. A W S states throughput of up to six times stock My S Q L and stock Postgres S Q L on similar hardware. Storage grows automatically, up to two hundred fifty-six tebibytes for a cluster volume. Aurora also automates clustering and replication, which are usually the hardest parts of database administration. You can move from R D S for My S Q L or Postgres S Q L with a snapshot or one-way replication. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, these figures come from the Aurora user guide. Exam tip: My S Q L or Postgres S Q L compatible, with higher performance and storage that grows by itself, means Aurora.

1.title: Amazon DynamoDB: Serverless NoSQL
1.text: Amazon Dynamo D B is a serverless, fully managed no S Q L database for key-value and document data. It delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. There are no servers to provision or patch, and no maintenance windows. On-demand capacity charges per request and scales up and down, and provisioned capacity is the alternative. Data is copied across three Availability Zones by default, and global tables replicate across Regions. Data is encrypted at rest by default, with point-in-time recovery for up to thirty-five days. D A X adds an in-memory cache, taking responses from milliseconds to microseconds. One limit to remember: Dynamo D B has no join operator. Exam tip: key-value lookups, milliseconds at any scale and no servers means Amazon Dynamo D B.

1.title: Amazon ElastiCache: In-Memory Caching
1.text: Amazon ElastiCache is a managed in-memory data store and cache. Its engines are Valkey, Memcached and Redis O S S. Put it in front of a database, so popular reads come from memory. That is faster for users, and it means less load on the database. In the figure, the application asks the cache first. A hit returns data straight from memory. A miss reads the database, then stores the answer in the cache for next time. ElastiCache Serverless needs only a name, and node-based clusters give control over node type, node count and Availability Zones. A W S manages hardware, monitoring, node replacement and patching. Exam tip: speeding up repeated reads with an in-memory cache means Amazon ElastiCache.

2.title: Amazon DocumentDB and Amazon Neptune
2.text: Two specialist engines complete the list. Amazon Document D B is a fully managed document database, compatible with Mongo D B, so you can use the same code, drivers and tools. Its storage grows automatically, it supports up to fifteen replicas, and backups can be kept for up to thirty-five days. Think of it as J S O N-like documents. Amazon Neptune is a fully managed graph database for highly connected data. You query it in Gremlin, open Cypher and S P A R Q L. Typical uses are recommendation engines, fraud detection and knowledge graphs, and it supports up to fifteen read replicas. Think of it as relationships. Exam tip: Mongo D B workloads mean Document D B; recommendations from relationships mean Neptune.

2.title: Moving Databases: AWS DMS and AWS SCT
2.text: Two services help you move a database. A W S Database Migration Service, D M S, migrates databases and data stores to A W S, or between the cloud and on-premises. It can do a one-time migration, or replicate ongoing changes to keep source and target in sync. It supports migrations that keep the same engine and migrations that change engine. The A W S Schema Conversion Tool, S C T, converts the schema and code from one engine to another, such as Oracle to Postgres S Q L. D M S Schema Conversion can also convert source schemas. Look at the figure: S C T converts, then D M S moves the data and keeps replicating changes. Exam tip: when the engine is different, S C T converts the schema, and D M S moves the data.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Databases
2.text: Here is how the exam frames databases. E C two or R D S: you run the database, or A W S manages it. Multi-A Z or read replica: failover, or more read capacity. R D S or Aurora: standard engines, or My S Q L and Postgres S Q L compatible with cloud-built storage. Dynamo D B: key-value lookups with no servers. ElastiCache: an in-memory cache for repeated reads. Document D B or Neptune: Mongo D B documents, or connected data. And S C T or D M S: convert the schema, or move the data. Exam tip: match the data model and the management you want to the service.

2.title: Design Check: Tidewater's Database Plan
2.text: Now a design check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. The order database, without weekend patching: Amazon R D S. Keep running if a data center fails: a Multi-A Z deployment. Reports slowing the order database: a read replica. My S Q L compatible, with storage that grows itself: Amazon Aurora. Catalog lookups in milliseconds at any scale: Amazon Dynamo D B. Product pages read thousands of times a minute: Amazon ElastiCache. Recommendations from links between customers and products: Amazon Neptune. And an old Oracle database to Postgres S Q L: S C T to convert, and D M S to move. Pause the video if you want more time.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. On managed or not: R D S patches, backs up and fails over for you, while on E C two you do it all. On availability and reads: Multi-A Z fails over, read replicas scale reads, and Aurora is My S Q L and Postgres S Q L compatible. For no S Q L and speed: Dynamo D B for key-value at any scale, and ElastiCache for in-memory caching. For specialist engines: Document D B for Mongo D B documents, and Neptune for graphs. And for migration: S C T converts the schema, and D M S moves the data.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Tidewater runs a My S Q L database on an E C two instance and wants A W S to handle patching, backups and failover. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C, Amazon R D S for My S Q L. R D S runs My S Q L as a managed service, so A W S handles database and operating system patching, backups and failover. Dynamo D B, ElastiCache and Neptune use different data models, and would not run the existing My S Q L database.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Tidewater's order database must stay available if one Availability Zone fails. Which R D S feature meets this need? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A, a Multi-A Z deployment with a synchronous standby in another zone. It fails over automatically. A read replica scales reads, a bigger instance does not remove the single zone, and a nightly snapshot restores slowly, with data loss.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. The product catalog must answer simple key lookups with single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, with no servers to manage. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B, Amazon Dynamo D B, with on-demand capacity. It is a serverless no S Q L database with single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. R D S and Aurora are relational engines with instances to size, and Neptune is built for connected data.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. The same product pages are read thousands of times a minute and slow the database. Which service can serve those repeated reads from memory? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D, Amazon ElastiCache. It is a managed in-memory data store and cache, so repeated reads come from memory and the database does less work. Document D B stores documents, and D M S and S C T are migration tools.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Select two. Tidewater is moving an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora Postgres S Q L. Which two services help? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Moving between different engines needs the schema converted, which the A W S Schema Conversion Tool does, and the data moved, which A W S Database Migration Service does. ElastiCache is a cache, Neptune is a graph database, and A W S Backup protects data rather than migrating it.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: C. Question two: A. Question three: B. Question four: D. Question five: A and C. That completes Module nine. Next, Module ten covers networking and content delivery: the V P C, connectivity options, Route fifty-three and CloudFront.
